sector: Grassroots amateur football club refreshing its playing kit, crest and shirt numbering through one local kit supplier.
founded_place_size: Founded 1974, a village near Cirencester in the Cotswolds, with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups.
about: Ridgeway Rovers are a village football club that has worn the same crest since 1974 and drawn their own shirt numbering since the nineties. This season brings the first new shirt since 2019. The club wants its own crest and its own hand drawn numbering back as proper artwork, so any supplier can print it and it still looks like Ridgeway.
audience: Players and parents at twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt, often buying a child's fourth kit in five years, who want something that looks like a proper club.
price_positioning: Grassroots, twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt printed by one local supplier. Numbering has to reduce to a single robust cuttable colour for heat press and flock, honest rather than pro tier.

palette.name: Claret
palette.role: mandatory on the kit sheet, as the 2 pt rule beneath every heading; not printed in the master crest
palette.usage: The 2 pt rule locked beneath every 30 pt heading on the kit sheet, as the type system requires; at most a short caption on Shirt White, as on ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf; the claret home shirt; one of the four kit colours for the single-ink and reversed crests and the glyphs. In the master crest the claret is the unprinted shirt cloth, as in ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg. Never a keyline.

palette.name: Navy
palette.role: mandatory in the master crest and on the kit sheet
palette.usage: The shield field of the crest, as stitched in ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg; on the kit sheet, headings, body and fine print on Shirt White, and any header band, as on ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf; the navy away shirt.

palette.name: Shirt White
palette.role: mandatory in the master crest and on the kit sheet
palette.usage: The ring lettering, 1974 and ring rules of the crest, as stitched in ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg; the kit sheet's page ground, as on ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf; all type on a Navy or Claret ground.

palette.name: Old Gold
palette.role: mandatory in the master crest; optional accent on the kit sheet
palette.usage: The ram's head and the shield border of the crest, as stitched in ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg; on the kit sheet's page design, a short label on a Navy or Claret ground or a thin rule only, as the header label and rule on ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf. Never a ground, body text, keyline or second colour on numbering or lettering.

palette.name: Pitch Green
palette.role: optional accent, thin rules on the kit sheet page design only
palette.usage: A thin rule on the kit sheet page design only, never type. It is not among the kit colours in ridgeway_supplier_note.txt, so it never appears on a crest, a glyph, a shirt-back name or number, or a garment.

typography: Ridgeway Rovers runs on two families. Headings are Champion Gothic Heavyweight, the condensed athletic gothic the club already uses: step 01 sets caps at 30 pt on 32 pt with tracking at 0 units because the line is optically fitted to fill its column edge to edge, and a 2 pt Claret rule locks directly beneath it, the same line setting at 44 px on 47 px on screen. Step 02 keeps the same face and caps at 18 pt on 20 pt with tracking at +10 units, a size invented because the existing prose names none, held at roughly 0.6 of the heading so it reads as a section marker and carrying no rule beneath it. Text is Freight Sans Pro: step 03 is Book at 9.5 pt on 13 pt, tracking 0 units, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, and step 04 is Medium at 7.5 pt on 10 pt with tracking at +15 units for size labels and print notes. Shirt numbers and the crest ring are never set in any typeface.
voice: Straightforward, warm, club room plain. Example line: Same crest we have worn since 1974, cleaned up so any printer can do it justice.
brand_assets_status: No artwork survives. The former kit secretary took the crest files when he moved away, leaving only a parent's phone photo of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. The numbering exists only as two marker on graph paper sheets, an alphabet and a digit set, drawn by a founding member in the nineties and photographed on a kitchen table. Last season's supplier back of shirt sheet is on hand as the format.
values: Keeping what is genuinely theirs, the 1974 crest and the founder's numbering, and reading as a real village club rather than a franchise or a school project.

scale.tracking: 0 units, width set by optical fit
scale.note: Caps only. The line is optically fitted so it fills its column edge to edge, so width comes from the fit and never from added tracking. A 2 pt Claret rule locks directly beneath. On screen the same line sets at 44 px on 47 px.

Size invented, none stated in the existing prose. Held at roughly 0.6 of the 30 pt heading so it reads as a section marker, not a second headline. Caps, fitted to the column but without the 2 pt rule, which belongs to the heading alone.

scale.sample: So any supplier can print it and it still looks like Ridgeway.
scale.note: Both numbers already stated in the existing prose and carried over unchanged.

scale.sample: ONE COLOUR · HEAT PRESS AND FLOCK
scale.note: This is the size label and print note setting. 7.5 pt comes from the existing prose; leading and the slight positive tracking are added so small caps stay legible on a supplier sheet.

type_system.signature_move: Every sheet is headed by one line of Champion Gothic Heavyweight caps at 30 pt on 32 pt, optically fitted to fill the column edge to edge, with a 2 pt Claret rule locked directly beneath it. Step 01 carries that behaviour and nothing else in the scale is allowed to imitate it.
rules: Never set a shirt number or the crest ring in any typeface. Both are drawn artwork.
Every heading is caps and is optically fitted to fill its column edge to edge. Width comes from the optical fit, never from added tracking.
A 2 pt Claret rule locks directly beneath every heading, on every sheet.
Headings set at 30 pt in print and 44 px on screen. No other heading size exists.
Only step 02 may use the display face without the Claret rule beneath it.
Numbering artwork must still reduce to a single robust cuttable colour for heat press and flock, so type set beside it stays one colour too.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels on the kit sheet are Shirt White, with Navy allowed for a header band, as on ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf; garments keep their own kit colour. On Shirt White, headings, body and fine print are Navy, Claret sets at most a short caption, and every 30 pt heading carries the 2 pt Claret rule. On Navy or Claret, type is Shirt White, or Old Gold for a short label. On the page design, outside the crests, glyphs and garments, Old Gold is for short labels and thin rules and Pitch Green for thin rules only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area outside the crests and glyphs, never a ground or body text. The crests, the glyphs and the shirt-back name and number use only Claret, Navy, Old Gold and Shirt White: the master crest Navy, Old Gold and Shirt White as stitched in ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg, with the claret cloth left unprinted; the reversed crest no more than three of them; the single-ink crest one; and each glyph, name or number one.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour in the crests, the glyphs or the kit sheet, and no scrim, gradient or translucent band of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: a caption sits beside or below the photograph as a solid block.
palette_rules.forbidden: No gradient, inline, keyline, outline or second colour on any shirt number, shirt-back name or glyph, as ridgeway_supplier_note.txt rules. Pitch Green never appears on a crest, a glyph, a shirt-back name or number, or a garment. No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or icons on the kit sheet, and none outside the four kit colours on the crests and glyphs.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs appear only as garment mock-ups on the kit sheet. Any shirt photograph shown there reads as its kit colour, the home shirt Claret #6B1F2E and the away shirt Navy #1E2A44, and is not otherwise recoloured.
